entities.name: Achille Marie Joseph Glorieux
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Achille Marie Joseph Glorieux (1910–1990) was a Belgian bishop and significant figure at the Second Vatican Council, where he served as secretary of the Mixed Commission that drafted Gaudium et Spes, the council's pivotal pastoral constitution on the Church in the modern world. Ordained a priest of the Société des Auxiliaires des Missions, he became Bishop of Namur and brought to the council both pastoral experience and a commitment to dialogue with contemporary culture.

Glorieux's role as secretary of the commission responsible for Schema XIII—eventually Gaudium et Spes—placed him at the centre of what many regarded as Vatican II's most ambitious and controversial document. The constitution engaged directly with questions of human dignity, economic justice, marriage, culture, and war, requiring sustained negotiation among theologians and bishops of widely divergent views. Glorieux helped manage this complex process, ensuring the text reached its final promulgation in December 1965.

His career embodied the Belgian Church's distinctive contribution to twentieth-century Catholicism: rigorous theology, social engagement, and openness to ecumenical and cultural dialogue. Belgium produced an outsized share of Vatican II's influential bishops and periti, and Glorieux stood among the most administratively significant of them. Gaudium et Spes remains one of the most cited and debated documents of the council, giving his secretarial work an enduring theological legacy.
